# Table label context isolation

Original OOXML generated by `tools/table_label_context_fixture.py`, reusing
only the independently authored package shell from the earlier label control.
No corpus text/artwork, font programs or third-party document engine is used.
Six pages isolate exact/minimum row height, explicit/omitted automatic line
spacing, inherited table borders cleared at table level and reinstated on
cells, nesting inside a padded cell, and complex-script font size on Latin
text. The label is the independently authored `W:` measurement string.

The source passes document/style/settings schemas. The reference application completed
all six detached table-range EMFs through an exact running-object-table lookup;
the source hash stayed unchanged and the document remained saved. Capture
metadata and hashes bind the binary drawing records to the reproducible source.
The controls contain text/font descriptors and border rectangles, not font
programs. `record_table_label_context.py` uses the bounded native-record guards
and checks the specific first-cell top border in every capture.

Each label baseline is 142 logical drawing units below its inner top-border
centre, regardless of the varied property. Nested range coordinates shift,
but this relative measurement does not. The physical frame has hundredth-mm
rounding; native offsets are approximately 17.04pt, while the current browser
offset is 17.1337890625pt in all cases. The residual is below one 600-DPI
drawing unit (0.12pt); this is not a zero-error visual match claim. None of
these contexts reproduces the original classroom pack's approximately 0.536pt
PDF baseline discrepancy. Further native source/PDF positioning work remains.

`capture_open_table_prompt_metafiles.ps1 -ExpectedControls 0` reproduces the
six already helper-opened saved ranges into fresh scratch outputs. It does not
open another document, export a PDF or change application/document state. The
separate PDF export remains live and has no completed reference; do not use
partial outputs or restart it solely because observation times out.

Local evidence tests reconstruct the native measurements and regenerate the
source byte-for-byte. The browser test clicks/types in every label, exports
each edit, preserves unrelated package parts, and restores every source part
exactly after one undo. All 13 browser exports pass schemas. The broader
100-case row-height/margin/spacing cohort passes cumulatively: four tests that
exceeded the initial concurrent five-second timeout pass serially with a
30-second test-only timeout. Build and license checks pass. No renderer code
or timing adjustment is included.

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 properties: §17.3.1.33 (spacing), §17.3.2.38 (sz),
§17.4 (table, row, cell, margin and border properties). No normative reference/spec
contradiction or completed corpus entry is asserted by these controls.
